Leave is applied for, approved and counted in Podium. Your balance is worked out from a ledger of credits and leave taken; nobody types it. Payroll still runs in RazorpayX: HR enters the unpaid days there by hand from a report in Podium.

What it’s for
Apply, approve, balances, unpaid days.
Read or act?
Act.
Who
Employee Manager HR Admin
Where
People → Leave, /leave. HR: Admin → Leave Settings, /admin/leave.

Who is covered

Leave covers Fraternitas staff on RazorpayX payroll, interns included. Floor staff on Redline attendance are not covered. If you are not covered, Leave shows “Leave is not set up for you in Podium”; ask HR. A manager who is not covered still sees the team half of the page.

HR turns leave on or off per person: open their edit form and set Leave policy to Fraternitas or Not covered.

Balances

The tiles at the top of Leave show what you can take.

  • Privilege leave (PL): 1.5 days credited each month, on the 1st.
  • Sick leave (SL): 1 day credited each month, on the 1st.
  • Period leave: shown only to people recorded as female. 1 day a month, does not build up.
  • Optional holiday: 1 a year, from the optional list.

PL and SL tiles show available, your balance and how far you can borrow. A red tile means the balance is negative. A joiner who starts on or before the 15th earns that month in full; after the 15th, the first credit is next month. Monthly credits begin from the cutover month HR sets; before that, your opening balance stands in.

Applying for leave

  1. Open Leave and find Apply for leave or work from home.
  2. Pick the Type: Privilege leave, Sick leave, Period leave, Optional holiday or Work from home.
  3. Set the dates. From, and To (leave empty for one day). For one day, Day is Full day, First half or Second half. For a range, First day is Full day or From second half, and Last day is Full day or Until first half. Optional holiday: pick one from the list. Period leave: one day, with Date.
  4. Reason is optional. Only your approver and HR see it.
  5. Check the count that appears under the form, then press Request leave. Your approver is emailed.
  • The day count is live. Weekends and fixed holidays are free: only working days (Monday to Friday) count. A holiday on a weekend gives no day in lieu.
  • PL must start today or later. SL can be applied up to 7 days back.
  • A request cannot cross 31 December, covers at most 60 working days, and cannot overlap another pending or approved request.
  • Upcoming holidays sits beside the form.

HR can record leave for someone else with the For picker on the form. It still goes to their approver.

Borrowing ahead, and unpaid days

If you ask for more PL or SL than your balance, the line under the form says so before you submit.

  • Borrowed ahead: the balance goes negative, up to what you will still earn by 31 December. Later monthly credits pay it back first.
  • Unpaid: anything beyond that is unpaid (loss of pay, LOP). It still needs approval.
⚠ Unpaid days reach payroll

Approved unpaid days go on the HR payroll report below. They are not taken from your balance.

Withdraw and cancel

  • Pending: press Withdraw in My requests.
  • Approved, not started: press Cancel. The days go back to your balance.
  • Started: “Started: ask your manager to cancel”. Your approver, their manager or HR cancels it.

Approving Manager

Requests from your team appear in Waiting for you. Each shows the dates, the day count, any borrowed or unpaid days, the person’s PL and SL, and their reason. Press Approve, or Reject (a note is required and they see it).

  • Your manager can also decide your team’s requests, to cover you when you are away. HR can too. Nobody can decide their own leave.
  • If the balance changed since the person applied, Podium reloads and shows today’s split. Check it and decide again.
  • With no manager, a founder’s leave goes to the other founder; anyone else’s goes to HR.

Who’s out Manager HR

The Who’s out (and who works from home) card is a calendar for your team. Switch Week or Month, step with the arrows, or press Today. Gold is leave, a lighter shade is pending; half days fill half the cell; weekends and fixed holidays are greyed. Below it, each request has a Cancel button for approved leave.

Work from home

Pick Work from home as the Type. It uses no balance, never counts as leave and never reaches payroll. It is approved by your manager’s manager (your manager if you have no skip-level; HR if you have no manager). The form names the approver. It shows on the calendar in blue, marked WFH.

Maternity and paternity HR

These are granted by HR; they are not on the apply form and use no balance. In Grant maternity / paternity leave pick the person, the type and the start date, then press Grant. It is approved at once and the person is emailed.

  • Maternity: 26 weeks (182 calendar days). The person must be recorded as female. A note is required: record the eligibility check (80 days worked in the last 12 months).
  • Paternity: 15 working days (weekends and fixed holidays are free). The person must be recorded as male.
  • If gender is not recorded, fill it in the profile first. You cannot grant your own.
  • Either may cross 31 December. Ends on is optional and defaults to the full length; set it when you already know the actual end. Returning early? Cancel it from the team view and grant again with the actual end date. The person sees “Granted by HR: ask HR to change or end it”.

HR tools HR

Open Leave Settings under Admin.

Cutover

The month monthly credits start from. It can only move earlier once credits exist. Press Save.

Holidays

Date, name and Fixed or Optional. Add with Add; rename or delete future ones only. A change after a request is approved does not recount it; Podium tells you how many requests include the date. Add next year’s list before January.

Covered people

Each person’s PL and SL, and whether the opening is set. Balance opens the entry: the first time per type it is Set opening (once); after that it is Adjust, a plus or minus in steps of 0.5 with a required note. Ledger lists every credit and debit.

Payroll: unpaid days HR

Payroll — unpaid days is at the top of Leave Settings. Pick the month (it opens on this month). It lists each person with unpaid days: code, RazorpayX id, name, days and the dates. Unpaid days fall on the last working days of the request. Enter these in RazorpayX by hand. Podium does not push them.

  1. Clear the warning. If requests touching the month are still pending, a banner names them. Decide them before payroll.
  2. Download CSV and enter the figures in RazorpayX. A “missing” RazorpayX id needs fixing in the profile.
  3. Press Mark exported. Podium keeps a snapshot.
  4. Watch for changes. If a cancel or late approval changes the month after the export, the card lists who (was, now). Carry the difference into next month’s payroll.
ⓘ Exits are not here

A negative balance at exit is settled in the F&F, not on this report. A holiday added after approval can flag a row: check its dates.

Year end

  • PL carries up to 5 days. The rest lapses. A negative balance carries as it is.
  • SL lapses in full.
  • This happens by itself on the first look at balances in January.

HR From 1 November to 31 January, Year end in Leave Settings previews each person’s projected PL and SL at 31 December, what PL carries and what lapses. It is read only: balance plus credits still to come, less pending requests.

Exits

On the exit checklist, the Leave balance confirmed line fills itself. It shows PL and SL at the last working day (including credits still to land that month), and notes that SL is not paid out. A negative balance is unpaid days in the F&F settlement; positive PL is shown, and Finance decides on encashment.

  • HR cannot mark the line Done while a request is pending, or while leave runs past the last working day. Cancel or decide it first.
  • Done saves the figures on the exit. Reopening clears them.
  • For someone not covered, HR confirms the balance by hand.

parts.subtitle: Your own performance page, the team feed, and the twice-yearly appraisal cycle from self-review to acknowledgement.

chapters.title: My Performance
chapters.html:
My Performance is your own corner of Podium: the wins you've recorded, the observations and 1:1 notes that have been shared with you, the open action items from your meetings, and your live appraisal. Everyone has this page, even with no other access, and it always shows only your own data.

What it’s for
Your record, in one place.
Read or act?
Act: record your own wins; take part in your appraisal.
Who
Employee Manager HR Admin
Scope
Always just you.

The Appraisals block

When there's a live appraisal cycle that involves you, a yellow Appraisals block sits at the top. It's your one-click way in, and it's how you take part without needing any special menu:

  • Your own appraisal: “start your self-review,” “self-review submitted (editable),” or “your result is ready” once HR shares it. Click through to the appraisal screen.
  • Reviews you owe: if you manage people, anyone of yours waiting on your manager review appears here too.

If there's no active cycle, the block simply isn't shown. The full walkthrough is in Filling In an Appraisal.

Open action items

If your 1:1s have left you with action items that aren't done yet, they're gathered into a banner near the top, each tagged with the meeting it came from. It's a running to-do list pulled straight from your check-ins, so nothing quietly slips.

The three tabs

My Wins

Accomplishments you record about yourself. Click Add win, give it a title (and optional detail, a date and tags), and save. These are yours to add and edit, and they're the raw material for your self-review at appraisal time.

Shared With Me

Observations your managers (or HR) have explicitly chosen to share with you. You only ever see observations on this tier; the private and managers-only ones never appear here.

My 1:1s

Your one-to-one notes: the shared notes your manager wrote and the action items, which you can read. You can't edit a 1:1 (your manager owns it), and the manager-only private notes never show.

✓ Record wins as they happen

The best time to log a win is right after it lands, not the night before your self-review. A steady trickle through the year makes the appraisal write-up almost automatic, and gives your manager real examples to draw on.

ⓘ Why you can't see every note about you

“Shared With Me” shows only what was deliberately shared. Managers also keep constructive or work-in-progress observations at a more private setting while they're still forming a view. That's by design (see the Profile chapter for the visibility tiers); it isn't that something is being hidden from you unfairly, it's that not every working note is meant to be a finished message.

chapters.title: OKRs
chapters.html:
OKRs are how Podium tracks what we're trying to achieve each half-year and how far we've got. An Objective is a short, ambitious statement of intent; under it sit two to five Key Results — measurable checks that tell you whether the objective actually happened. They cascade from the company down to departments and individuals, run on the same twice-yearly rhythm as appraisals, and score themselves from your check-ins.

What it’s for
Set goals, track progress, grade the outcome.
Cadence
Two cycles a year (Apr & Oct), aligned to appraisals.
Who
Employee Manager HR Admin
Scope
Company & dept goals are open; individual goals stay within the reporting line.

The three levels

Company

The handful of goals the whole business is pushing on this cycle. Set by HR/leadership. Everyone can see them.

Department

A team's goals, ideally aligned up to a company objective. Set by HR or the department head. Everyone can see them.

Individual

Your own goals for the cycle, ideally aligned up to a department or company objective. You (or your manager) set them. Only you, your managers up the chain, and HR can see them — not your peers.

Key results & scoring

Each key result has a start, a target, and a live current value — or, for a yes/no result, a simple milestone. Its score is how far you've moved from start to target, capped between 0% and 100%. The objective's overall progress is the weighted average of its key results.

Two numbers matter: the auto progress (computed continuously from your check-ins) and, at the end, the final grade — a score you set yourself when the cycle moves to scoring, alongside a short reflection. The auto number is shown next to it for reference. Grading is deliberately a judgment call, not just the arithmetic.

Checking in

Open any objective and, on each key result, click Check in: enter the new current value, pick a confidence (On track / At risk / Off track), and add an optional note on what moved. Every check-in is kept as history, and the progress bar updates immediately.

✓ A weekly rhythm beats a scramble

Update your key results little and often. A result that hasn't been touched in a fortnight gets a Needs check-in flag on your My Performance page and on the cycle overview — a gentle nudge, not a telling-off.

Where OKRs live

OKRs

The overview: pick a cycle, then browse company, department and individual objectives with their progress. Click any objective to open it.

My Performance

Your My OKRs block — your objectives with quick check-in, a button to add a new objective, and the company/department goals surfaced to you.

Team

Managers see their reports' objectives and progress, and can drill into any of them.

The cycle, start to finish (HR)

HR runs cycles from OKRs → Manage cycles. A cycle moves through four states:

  • Draft — HR is building it and seeding company & department objectives; nobody else sees it yet.
  • Active — the working window. People add key results and check in; progress is live.
  • Scoring — end of cycle. Owners set the final grade and a reflection on each objective.
  • Closed — read-only archive.

OKRs & appraisals

Because a cycle is anchored to an appraisal date, the individual objectives for that period show up — read-only — on the appraisal screen, so the reviewer has the goals in front of them. They are context only and never change the rating or the increment.

chapters.title: Team
chapters.html:
Team is a manager's feed of recent activity across everyone who reports to them, directly or further down the line. It's where you keep an eye on your people's wins and observations, and where you quickly log a new observation without hunting through profiles.

What it’s for
Your team's recent performance activity.
Read or act?
Read; log observations inline.
Who
Manager HR Admin
Scope
Your whole reporting line.

Who shows up here

The feed covers your reporting chain: your direct reports and the people under them. If you don't manage anyone yet, the page says so; people appear here the moment they're set to report to you (on their profile).

Reading the feed

Each card is one piece of activity, newest first, tagged by type:

TypeWhat it shows
ObservationA note logged about the person, with its tone (Positive, Neutral, Constructive).
WinAn accomplishment the person recorded about themselves.
1:1A one-to-one's shared notes. If it's a 1:1 you're not party to, it shows as “Private 1:1” without the contents.

Click a card to jump to that person's profile. Two dropdowns at the top filter the feed: by type (just observations, just wins, just 1:1s) and by person.

Logging an observation

  1. Use the yellow “Log observation for…” dropdown and pick the person.
  2. Write what you observed and set its tone and its visibility (see the callout). Add a date and tags if useful.
  3. Save. It joins their record on their profile and your feed. Close the panel with the × when you're done.
⛔ Choose the visibility deliberately

Every observation has a visibility, and it decides who ever reads it: Private (you and HR only), Shared with managers (you, the chain above the person, and HR), or Shared with person (also the person themselves). The person never sees the first two. Pick before you save: get it right at the moment of writing rather than relying on fixing it later.

✓ Little and often beats a year-end scramble

A few honest observations spread through the period make calibration and the appraisal write-up far easier, and fairer, than trying to remember everything in one sitting. The inline logger is built so you can do it in the flow of a normal week.

chapters.title: Appraisals (HR)
chapters.html:
Appraisals is where HR runs the twice-yearly review from start to finish: create a cycle, choose who's in it, watch progress as self-reviews and manager reviews come in, calibrate the final ratings, and share results. This chapter covers the HR view; the form everyone fills in is covered in Filling In an Appraisal.

What it’s for
Running appraisal cycles.
Read or act?
Act: create, enroll, calibrate, share.
Who
HR Admin
Cadence
Twice a year: 1 Apr & 1 Oct.

How a cycle works

Cycles are anchored to an appraisal date, either 1 April or 1 October. That date is also when any increment takes effect. Everything else is worked out from it: the six-month review window, and the eligibility cut-off (three months before the anchor). A cycle moves through four states:

StatusWhat it means
DraftBeing set up. Enroll people here. No reviews accepted yet.
ActiveOpen for self-reviews and manager reviews.
CalibrationReviews locked; HR sets the final ratings and shares results.
ClosedDone and read-only.

Creating and enrolling

  1. New cycle. Pick the appraisal date (1 Apr / 1 Oct) and an optional name like “H2 2026.” The window and cut-off fill in themselves.
  2. Enroll people. Open enrollment to see everyone with their eligibility worked out for you. Eligible means they joined before the cut-off; borderline and missing-join-date cases are flagged for your judgement. Tick who's in and enroll them.
  3. Activate. Move the cycle to Active to open reviews. People now see their self-review on My Performance, and managers see the reviews they owe.
ⓘ Catch-up periods are automatic

Each person's review window runs from their last appraisal (or their joining date if it's their first) up to the anchor. So someone who joined mid-period, or missed a cycle, automatically gets a longer first window rather than being short-changed. Their increment is pro-rated to match.

The cycle dashboard

Opening a cycle shows progress tiles, Enrolled, Self done, Mgr done, Finalized, Shared, Acknowledged and a PIP count, so you can see at a glance where the cohort is. Below them is the calibration grid: one row per person showing their self rating, their manager's rating, the final rating, an HR-only note, and a suggested increment percentage.

Calibrating and sharing

  1. Move the cycle to Calibration when reviews are in. This locks further editing of the reviews.
  2. Set each final rating in the grid (1–5) and add an optional calibration note. The note is HR-internal and never shown to the employee. Click Finalize.
  3. Share results. Use Share all finalized to release every finalized result at once, or share one at a time from a person's appraisal. Only then can the employee see their rating.
  4. Close the cycle when everyone's done.
⛔ Nothing reaches the employee until you Share

Self-ratings, manager ratings, your calibration note and the final rating all stay hidden from the employee until the moment you share. The employee never sees the manager's raw rating or your note, only the final rating and the manager's written feedback. Share deliberately, and only once a result is genuinely finalized.

⚠ A low final rating triggers a PIP

If a final rating falls at or below the threshold (2 by default), the appraisal is flagged as a Performance Improvement Plan and counted on the PIP tile. That's a deliberate, visible outcome, so set final ratings with care.

chapters.title: Filling In an Appraisal
chapters.html:
This is the single appraisal screen everyone uses, but it shows you a different face depending on who you are to it: the person being appraised, their manager, or HR. You reach it from the link on My Performance (for your own or one you owe) or from the cycle grid (for HR). It shows you exactly the part you need to fill in, and hides the rest until it's meant to be seen.

What it’s for
One person's appraisal, end to end.
Read or act?
Act: write, rate, calibrate, acknowledge.
Who
Employee Manager HR Admin
Scale
1–5 plus three written prompts.

The flow, in order

An appraisal moves through clear stages, each unlocking the next: self-review → manager review → HR calibration → shared with you → acknowledged. You only ever act on the stage that's yours.

If it's your appraisal Employee

  1. Give yourself an overall rating from 1 to 5, using the rating buttons.
  2. Answer the three prompts in writing: what went well, what could have gone better, and your focus for the next period.
  3. Rate your KPIs if your role has them (optional).
  4. Submit. You can keep editing while the cycle is open; submitting also lets your manager start their review.

Once HR shares the result, this screen shows Your result: your final rating, your manager's written feedback, and any increment. You can optionally acknowledge it with a note, and open a printable letter.

If you're the manager Manager

You see the person's submitted self-review first, then your own form: an overall rating, the same three prompts, and optional per-KPI ratings. Submit when ready; like the self-review, it stays editable while the cycle is open. You do not set the final rating, that's HR's calibration step, and you won't see the final number until it's finalized.

ⓘ The three prompts

Every review, self and manager, answers the same three questions: what went well, what could have gone better, and the focus for the next period. Keeping the prompts identical on both sides makes the two views easy to compare side by side at calibration.

If you're HR HR

You see both reviews in full, then the calibration panel:

  1. Set the final rating (1–5) and an optional calibration note. The note is HR-internal and never shown to the employee. Click Finalize.
  2. Record the increment if you have compensation access: an increment percentage and/or a one-time bonus. The effective date defaults to the cycle's anchor, and the suggested percentage comes from the rating band.
  3. Share with the employee. Until you do, they see nothing.
  4. Print the letters. An appraisal letter, and an increment letter where there's a revision, open as clean printable pages you can save as PDF.
⛔ The calibration note stays with HR

The calibration note is for HR's own record only. It is never shown to the employee or the manager, even after sharing. Use it for context behind a decision; never put anything in it you'd be uncomfortable keeping internal.

ⓘ Increments while the vault is off

With the salary vault disabled (the current default), an increment records the percentage and any bonus amount, not an absolute salary. The increment letter states the revision in those terms. Absolute figures only come into play once the vault is switched on, after the extra security layer is live (see Settings).

chapters.title: Analytics
chapters.html:
Analytics is the numbers view of Podium: how the team is growing, what it costs, and how performance is trending. Everything on this page is a total or an average: it never shows any individual person’s pay or rating.

What it’s for
Org, cost & performance trends.
Read or act?
Read-only.
Who
HR Admin
Extra gate
Payroll Cost: salary allow-list only.

The three sections

SectionWhat it shows
Org & HeadcountHeadcount by department and type, joiners vs exits by month, how long people have been here, and the attrition rate.
Payroll CostTotal annual CTC and the monthly cost it implies, cost by department, salary spread, and a plan-vs-actuals trend that fills in as real payouts are recorded. Only visible to the salary allow-list.
PerformanceRating spread and participation for recent appraisal cycles, PIP count, and how actively observations, wins and 1:1s are being logged.
ⓘ Aggregates only

The Payroll Cost section is department totals and averages. To see a specific person’s pay you still go to their profile, and that stays limited to the salary allow-list, with every view logged.

ⓘ Empty charts are normal at first

Cycle charts appear after the first appraisal cycle runs, and the “actuals” series fills in as payouts are recorded (automatically once the payroll connector is live). An empty chart means no data yet, not a fault.

parts.subtitle: The role and KPI registry and the department structure that the org chart and appraisals are built on.

chapters.title: Roles & KPIs
chapters.html:
Roles & KPIs is the registry of job roles at Legend of Toys: each role's title, level, job description, the responsibilities it carries, the KPIs it's measured on, and (for those with compensation access) its salary band. People are then assigned to a role on their profile, and the role's KPIs flow into their appraisal.

What it’s for
Defining job roles and their KPIs.
Read or act?
Read; HR edits; bands need comp access.
Who
Manager HR Admin
Feeds
Profiles & appraisal KPIs.

The role list

The main screen lists every role with its title, code, level, department, KPI count and (if you have compensation access) the mid-point of its salary band. A locked padlock in the band column means the bands exist but you don't have access to see them. Click a row to open the role.

A role's detail

Each role has two halves:

Job Definition

Title, code, level, department, a short summary, the full job description, and a list of responsibilities (one per line). HR edits these; everyone else reads them.

KPIs

The measures this role is judged on. Each KPI has a name, description, a type (quantitative or qualitative), a target and a weight. These are what appear, per person, in the appraisal.

Salary band

Minimum, mid and maximum for the role. Visible and editable only with compensation access; hidden behind a padlock for everyone else.

People in this role

Everyone currently assigned to the role, each a link to their profile.

Creating and editing (HR)

  1. New Role on the list: enter a title (and optional code and level) to create it, then you land on its detail to flesh it out.
  2. Fill in the definition and click Save definition. Mark a role inactive rather than deleting it when it's no longer in use.
  3. Add KPIs with Add KPI, fill in each one, then Save KPIs (the definition and the KPIs save separately).
✓ Good KPIs make better appraisals

Because a role's KPIs are exactly what both the employee and the manager rate at appraisal time, time spent here pays off later. Clear names, a real target and sensible weights turn a vague review into a specific one.

ⓘ Why a band might show a padlock

Salary bands sit behind the separate compensation permission, just like pay on a profile. If you can manage roles but see a padlock on the bands, that's expected: an admin can grant compensation access if you need it.

chapters.title: Departments
chapters.html:
Departments is the list of teams at Legend of Toys, each with a head, an optional parent department, and a live headcount. It's the structure the directory filters by, the dashboard counts by, and that profiles and roles attach to.

What it’s for
Defining the team structure.
Read or act?
Read; HR adds & edits.
Who
Manager HR Admin
Feeds
Directory, dashboard, profiles.

The list

Each row shows the department's name, code, its head, its parent department (if it sits under another), and its current headcount. The headcount updates as people are assigned to or moved off the department on their profiles.

Adding or editing (HR)

  1. New Department (or the pencil to edit one) opens a small form.
  2. Set the name (the only required field), and optionally a code, a head (chosen from people), a parent department and a description.
  3. Use the Active toggle to retire a department without deleting it.
  4. Save.
ⓘ Parent department vs reporting line

The parent department nests teams for grouping (for example a Store team under Production). It is not the same as the org chart's reporting lines, which come from each person's manager, not from their department. The two can look similar but are set in different places.

✓ Set a head where you can

Naming a department head keeps the structure legible and gives the org chart and reports a clear owner per team. It's optional, but a department with no head is easy to lose track of.

parts.subtitle: Who can see and do what in Podium, and the system-wide settings.

chapters.title: Roles & Permissions
chapters.html:
Roles & Permissions is where an admin defines what people can do in Podium. Podium runs its own set of roles, separate from every other LOT system, built from four simple permissions. You create as many named roles as you like from those permissions, then hand them out on the Users screen.

What it’s for
Defining Podium access roles.
Read or act?
Act: create & edit roles.
Who
Admin
Scope
Podium only, not other systems.

The four permissions

PermissionWhat it unlocks
ViewThe directory, org chart and dashboards. The baseline for seeing anyone beyond yourself.
People (HR)Manage people, departments, roles, documents and org snapshots, and run appraisal cycles.
CompensationSee and edit pay: increments, bonuses and salary bands. Kept separate so it can be granted on its own.
AdminManage these roles, assign people to them, and change settings.

Creating a role

  1. New Role. Give it a key (a short code like hr_lead), a readable label and an optional description.
  2. Flip on the permissions it should carry. A role with none of them is a perfectly valid “self-only” role.
  3. Save, then assign people to it on the Users screen.
⚠ Any higher permission switches View on for you

If you turn on People, Compensation or Admin, the View permission is switched on and locked automatically. That's deliberate: those jobs all need to see people in the first place, so a role can't accidentally be created that locks itself out of the screens it's meant to use.

System roles

Two roles come built in and can't be reshaped: Admin (everything) and Employee (the empty, self-only default). You can rename their label and description, but not their permissions, and you can't delete them. A handful of ready-made roles (an HR preset, a compensation preset, a people-manager preset) are also provided to copy or use as-is.

⛔ Podium roles don't touch other systems

Giving someone the HR or Admin role here changes only their People & Performance access. It does not change anything they can do in Garage, Redline or any other LOT system; those are governed separately. This isolation is the whole reason Podium has its own roles. A role with people assigned to it also can't be deleted, so reassign first.

chapters.title: Users
chapters.html:
Users is where an admin hands out Podium roles. Every LOT person with a login appears in one list; you pick a Podium role for each. Anyone left without a role gets self-only access, which is a real, working level, just their own profile and wins.

What it’s for
Assigning a Podium role to each person.
Read or act?
Act: set one role per person.
Who
Admin
Default
No role = self-only.

Reading the list

Each row is a person with a login: their name, email, their current Podium role (or “self-only (default)” if none), and a dropdown to change it. A search box up top filters by name, email or role.

Assigning a role

  1. Find the person with the search box.
  2. Pick a role from their dropdown. The list is the roles you defined on Roles & Permissions.
  3. That's it. The change saves immediately. To remove someone's access back to baseline, choose — none (self-only) —.
ⓘ Accounts come from Garage; this only sets People access

You don't create logins here; LOT accounts are made in Garage. The Users screen only decides what a person can do in Podium. So a brand-new joiner has a login as soon as Garage sets it up, and self-only access in Podium until you give them a wider role.

⚠ One Podium role per person

Each person has exactly one Podium role at a time, so picking a new one replaces the old. If someone needs an unusual mix of access, the answer is to define a role with that mix on Roles & Permissions and assign it, rather than trying to stack roles.

✓ Manager access doesn't need a role

Remember that seeing your team comes from the org chart, not from a role here. You don't need to assign anyone a “manager” role for them to see their reports; just make sure people's managers are set on their profiles. Roles here are for the wider tiers: HR, compensation and admin.

chapters.title: Settings
chapters.html:
Settings holds the handful of system-wide switches that change how Podium behaves for everyone: the salary vault, the appraisal eligibility rule, and the shortcuts into the permission screens. It's a short page, but a couple of its switches are consequential.

What it’s for
System-wide settings.
Read or act?
Act: a few global toggles.
Who
Admin
Scope
The whole of Podium.

Salary Vault

This switch decides whether Podium stores absolute salary figures at all. While it's off (the default), Podium records only increment percentages and one-time bonus amounts; full base-salary and CTC figures are never kept. Turning it on lets those figures be stored and shown to people with compensation access.

⛔ Leave the vault off until the security layer is live

Company-wide standing pay is the most sensitive data we hold, so the vault is meant to stay off until an extra sign-in wall (a network-level access layer in front of the whole site) is in place. Do not switch it on as a convenience: turning it on early would store full salaries before that protection exists. Until then, percentages and bonuses cover what appraisals need.

Appraisal Eligibility

A single number: the minimum tenure, in days, before someone counts as eligible for an appraisal. It sets the bar that the enrollment screen uses when it works out who's eligible for a cycle. Edit the number and click away to save.

Permissions

A reminder that Podium runs its own permissions, with quick links to Roles & Permissions (define roles) and Users (assign them). Anyone with no role assigned gets self-only access. See those two chapters for the detail.

ⓘ These settings ripple outward

Unlike a personal preference, a switch here changes Podium for everyone. The eligibility number shapes who's offered in the next cycle; the vault setting changes what every compensation screen will store and show. Change them with that reach in mind.
